reviews.author: Hyukjun Kang
reviews.text:
As a student studying brand design, I usually use various cafe branding examples as reference. I would like to say that ‘Yeon Kissaten’, the third space following Hearts Coffee and Hearts Houtz, is a space where the owner’s unique aesthetic stands out. I liked that it went beyond the simple expansion that started with Hearts Coffee and presented a unique concept that harmoniously blended Korean sentiment and Japanese 'Kissaten' culture.
I was particularly impressed by the in-depth explanation of the essence of Kissaten, a ‘tea drinking shop’, through the linguistic concept of 緣 (relationship). By setting '緣', which means meeting and connection, as the main concept, we build an organic relationship between guests, space, tea and cuisine. Furthermore, kites, which are deeply rooted in Korean sentiment, were used as a visual metaphor to add depth to the space with a classic yet sophisticated aesthetic. In addition, I think that the unique menu category of small tables, which blends organically with the space called Kissaten, has a clear differentiating strength from other cafes. This is a place I want to visit again🩵🩵🩵

reviews.text: Although it is small in size, it is the perfect place to watch a performance up close. Live jazz is a very high quality performance with great acoustics and a fantastic atmosphere. Red lighting and elegant decorations create a professional atmosphere. The staff are friendly and professional and provide explanations of the pieces, making for a comfortable experience. But the food was a bit disappointing. Some of the dishes were not as described on the menu, the grilled brie in particular was disappointing and overall it did not live up to expectations. Drinks are expensive, with a small bottle of beer costing 12,000 to 15,000 yuan, and when you add the 15,000 yuan entrance fee, it becomes less cost-effective. The drum sound was sometimes so loud that it interfered with listening to the music. The average cost per person is 20,000-30,000 yuan, suitable for music lovers, and it is recommended to focus on listening to music rather than food. There is no waiting time, but wheelchair access is limited and vegetarian options are lacking. Overall, it's a great place to experience live jazz.
